blocks.text: # Archived planning record — Harvey/C&H single-agent route
## Supersession notice

This document preserves a prior Harvey/C&H route and its transport history. It is not the active research plan, must not authorize a run, and must not be used to characterize the current product benchmark. The completed STALE protocol remains in [STALE_PHASE1_PLAN.md](STALE_PHASE1_PLAN.md). The active product-benchmark protocol is [ARTIFACT_TRAVEL_V2_PLAN.md](ARTIFACT_TRAVEL_V2_PLAN.md), which evaluates the complete Proofpress handoff package against natural generic continuity through an A→B→independent-reviewer boundary.

The completed Harvey PSA slice remains a negative historical boundary. Its B0/C0/C3 records, the OpenRouter/Novita slice, C&H planning, and all multi-agent drafts remain immutable historical material; none is resumed, relabeled, or pooled into STALE or Artifact Travel v2.
## Motivation and claim boundary: static versus dynamic

Harvey tasks are difficult document-work tasks, but an official single-agent run normally need not create a handoff. The study therefore does not mislabel Harvey as already an agent-to-agent benchmark. Instead, it turns a Harvey task into a controlled, long-horizon workflow with meaningful intermediate products. A stage cannot simply tell the next stage “continue”: it hands off an evidence map, a decision/issue register, a draft, and an accepted work product.

The paper-level claim must stay narrow: for the evaluated tasks, model, and fixed workflow, document-native admitted provenance may improve the quality and cost of recovering prior decisions. It will not claim that all multi-agent systems improve legal work, that Proofpress proves legal correctness, or that a benchmark score is a production safety guarantee.
## Fixed runtime and workflow

The initial runtime is the open-source Harvey LAB v1.0 task and scoring harness, not a new benchmark. Its task directory, task instructions, tool contract, result packaging, and official rubric remain unchanged. Our wrapper schedules the fixed stages and materializes their handoff inputs at declared boundaries. The active transport is Vercel AI Gateway with exact `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` execution and exact `openai/gpt-5.6-terra` blind scoring; it may not change a task or scorer. Harvey remains the final-legal-deliverable baseline; it is not the sole long-term validation scenario. Static Harvey results estimate the present task slice only; the next benchmarks test persistent state, conflict, evidence lineage, and research-report continuity separately.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  D["Harvey task workspace\nsource documents + instructions"] --> O["Central orchestrator\nplan / delegate / synthesize"]
  O --> W1["Worker 1\nfinancial / commercial review"]
  O --> W2["Worker 2\nregulatory / environmental review"]
  O --> W3["Worker 3\ncontract / personnel review"]
  W1 --> S["Central synthesis / review\nfinal memo + tracker"]
  W2 --> S
  W3 --> S
  S --> R["Harvey official scorer"]
  O -. "ordinary coordination.md in C1/C2" .-> W1
  O -. "ordinary coordination.md in C1/C2" .-> W2
  O -. "ordinary coordination.md in C1/C2" .-> W3
  W1 -. "native lineage in C2 only" .-> S
  W2 -. "native lineage in C2 only" .-> S
  W3 -. "native lineage in C2 only" .-> S
```

The planning and synthesis calls are the same **orchestrator role**, invoked as fresh sessions—not two controllers. The workers do not message peers; they write specialist artifacts into the shared workspace and the orchestrator accepts, rejects, or merges their findings. `coordination.md` remains an ordinary mutable team file in both C1 and C2. Proofpress is deterministic carrier/verification code, not another model, and in C2 it records the lineage of selected artifacts and decisions without replacing normal collaboration state.
### Checkpoint contract

| Checkpoint | Producer | Required artifact | Receiver must be able to determine |
|---|---|---|---|
| P0 | Orchestrator | task plan and delegation map | scope, requested deliverable, worker domains, unresolved questions |
| W1–W3 | Specialist workers | domain findings / evidence artifacts | sources, claims, caveats, and domain-specific risk conclusions |
| D1 | Orchestrator | acceptance / merge decision register | which findings are accepted, rejected, superseded, or conditional and why |
| F1 | Orchestrator | final memo and tracker | consolidated claims, remaining uncertainty, and exact terminal deliverables |

Every arm produces the same semantic artifact contract. The treatment changes the **representation and verification of lineage**, not the task, source corpus, roles, tools, model, or maximum stage count. The initial end-to-end gates fix a no-revision path (five model stages); a later frozen matrix may declare a common revision cap.
### C3 hybrid checkpoint contract

In `C3 sas-proofpress`, the system schedules only semantically important checkpoints; it does not ask the agent to write a ledger after every step. The agent supplies the evidence, finding, status, rationale, and revision meaning in ordinary task output. Deterministic Proofpress code validates the carrier, anchors, references, and version/decision relationships, then commits the admitted update. The receiver reads the latest artifact head, open decisions, and relevant evidence references instead of replaying the full session or rereading all memory.

| Checkpoint | Required semantic payload | Proofpress admission check |
|---|---|---|
| E0 initial evidence extraction | evidence items, source locations, uncertainty | evidence references and artifact identity |
| F1 material finding | claim, supporting evidence, caveat, scope | finding-to-evidence links and new version |
| D1 accept/reject decision | disposition, rationale, alternatives, actor | decision status and parent finding lineage |
| X1 conflict or new evidence | changed evidence, conflict, proposed consequence | supersession, contradiction, and open-decision continuity |
| R1 draft | draft artifact and unresolved decisions | artifact head and claim/dependency coverage |
| V1 validation/revision | validation result, corrected claim, reversal reason | revision chain and justified reversal |
| T1 final artifact | terminal artifact, remaining uncertainty, open decisions | final head, decision completeness, and integrity |
## Accepted next matrix: architecture and communication

| Arm | Architecture / communication | What the agent receives | What it identifies |
|---|---|---|---|
| `B0 harvey-one-shot` | one Harvey agent; one continuous session; no handoff artifact | original task context and source workspace | original Harvey one-shot baseline |
| `C0 sas-ordinary` | one SAS agent; five fresh-session checkpoints; ordinary continuity | original task plus ordinary checkpoint artifact | fresh-session SAS ordinary control |
| `C1 centralized-memory` | centralized fan-out: orchestrator → 3 parallel workers → synthesis | ordinary worker artifacts + mutable `coordination.md` | normal shared-memory team baseline |
| `C2 centralized-memory-proofpress` | exactly C1 | C1 inputs plus native Proofpress lineage on key worker artifacts, adoption/merge decisions, and final artifacts | MAS + Proofpress |
| `C3 sas-proofpress` | one SAS agent with the same task flow as C0 | C0 inputs plus hybrid Proofpress checkpoints and latest-head/open-decision retrieval | SAS + Proofpress |

The active Proofpress estimand is `C3 − C0` (lineage increment within matched SAS). `C0 − B0` estimates the effect of fresh-session SAS/sessionization. `C3 − B0` is a mixed total difference and must never be reported as the Proofpress effect. C1/C2 and the architecture interaction remain a future MAS extension. All active contrasts require identical task, fixed model slug, source workspace, tool cap, and total billable-token cap; provider selection and fallback policy are frozen after qualification and recorded per call.

The static Harvey slice can still estimate whether decomposition is worthwhile, but a null `C0`/`C1` difference is not evidence that MAS or Proofpress lacks value in general: a strong SAS agent can read all static material in one session. Dynamic tasks are required to test stale conclusions, conflict, supersession, restart recovery, and revision cost. Raw-history and status ablations remain secondary diagnostics, not substitutes for C3.

`proofpress-no-status` is a later diagnostic ablation: preserve the text/rationale but remove source and decision status. It is not a first-wave official Harvey arm unless the mechanism gates show an effect worth decomposing further.
## Hypotheses and falsifiers

| ID | Hypothesis | Evidence needed | Falsified for this study if |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | Artifact-native Proofpress lineage improves criterion-level success relative to the same centralized team with ordinary shared memory. | paired per-criterion Harvey score plus deterministic provenance checks. | The paired estimate is null/negative or any criterion gain comes with more unsupported authority upgrades. |
| H2 | Proofpress reduces handoff/adoption error or coordination work at comparable quality without relying on extra billable tokens. | token ledger, latency, tool reads, adoption/recovery probes. | No operational measure improves after accounting for all prompt, memory, metadata, and artifact tokens. |
| H3 | A centralized fan-out workflow is not presumed to beat a single agent. | budget-neutral C0-versus-C1 architecture pilot. | reporting claims a decomposition benefit without the reference. |
| H4 | Lineage preserves justified reversals rather than making agents blindly follow history. | seeded or natural reversal conditions and decision checks. | It increases false blocks or reduces correct reversals materially. |
| H5 | DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 is a cost-appropriate fixed-model reference, not a universal best model. | observed Gate 1 criterion results, route metadata, and frozen next-slice configuration. | later reporting turns this operational selection into a cross-model quality claim. |
| H6 | Proofpress's main value in dynamic work is trustworthy continuity and recovery; quality or token gains may appear only when conflict, revision, or session restart is present. | dynamic-track recovery, stale-use, reversal, lineage, and token measures. | no reduction in stale-use or recovery failures despite valid checkpoint admission, or gains depend on forcing ledger writes at every step. |
No hypothesis is marked supported before the planned empirical runs and audit are complete.
## Task selection

The initial substrate is Harvey LAB v1.0, pinned to commit `1da4750171bc5a534960b3d82d15ba7fd2cf653f` and its upstream license. Gate 0 begins with two legal-work task families already identified in the local adapter manifest:

- `corporate-ma/review-data-room-red-flag-review`
- `real-estate/extract-psa-key-terms/scenario-01`

For the main matrix, select six task instances stratified across document volume, ambiguity, deliverable type, and reversal opportunity. Freeze task IDs, hashes, tool limits, and any decomposition-specific role templates before the first treatment run. Do not tune one arm's prompt after seeing its outputs; a role-template correction applies to every arm and restarts that preregistered slice.
## Model plan

All first-wave runs use Harvey's task/scoring harness and an explicit Vercel AI Gateway adapter. Pi is intentionally deferred. This keeps **harness constant** and transport auditable; the first paper may claim only the frozen model/benchmark slice, not cross-harness generalization.

| Phase | Models | Arms | Tasks | Attempts | Purpose |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Completed transport prototype | DeepSeek 0731, Muse Spark 1.2, GPT-5.6 Luna | external `memory` vs `provenance.md` | 2 | 3 | operational result; not product-form treatment evidence |
| Archived Gateway qualification | DeepSeek 0731, GLM 5.2, Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite | B0, C0, C3 as available | PSA | historical | immutable transport evidence; no failed/incomplete slice is resumed, pooled, or interpreted |
| Active staged qualification | Luna execution + Terra scorer via Gateway, OpenAI-only/no-fallback | B0, C0, C3 | PSA | 3 staged trials | trial 1 executes all conditions concurrently, then undergoes operational analysis; only a clean analysis permits parallel trials 2/3 and blind Terra grading |
| Harvey formal matrix | separately frozen after all three staged trials grade cleanly | B0, C0, C3 | M&A + PSA | separately authorized | no formal estimand is implied by the qualification slice |
| STATE-Bench + MemConflict | separately frozen Gateway configuration | C0, C3 | benchmark-specific | benchmark-specific | independent persistent-state and conflict reports; never pooled |
| HiEviDR-Bench + DeepResearch Bench | separately frozen Gateway configuration | C0, C3 | benchmark-specific | benchmark-specific | adapter/scorer gates first, then independent evidence/research slices |

Each workflow run in the active slice uses exact `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` at `high` effort; every official scorer call uses exact `openai/gpt-5.6-terra` at `high` effort. Both are pinned to OpenAI only with fallback disabled, the same timeout/retry/tool policy, and separate execution/scoring cost ledgers. Proofpress is deterministic materialization/verification code and never makes a model call. At execution freeze, each row must record requested/resolved model, actual Gateway provider, `usage.cost`, fallback status/metadata, token values, latency, endpoint/adapter version, date, and pricing basis. Never substitute a `latest` alias, a local `$0` cost, or an unrecorded fallback.

The GLM 5.2 and Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite PSA slices are immutable, unqualified transport history: dynamic routing produced 500s or an incompatible provider output limit, and their records are retained without pooling. Luna/Terra v1 likewise remains immutable after its pre-inference parameter failure. V2 and the independent scorer-extension roots are the completed PSA run; transient scorer 500s were retried in new roots with no provider fallback. No historical transport record is pooled into the final analysis.

The active frozen model pair is `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` for execution and `openai/gpt-5.6-terra` for scoring through Vercel AI Gateway. Each call must resolve to the actual provider `openai`; a different provider, fallback, missing numeric cost, or incomplete telemetry is disqualifying. The old Novita/DeepInfra/DeepSeek/GLM/Gemini records are archived operational history, not a provider choice or comparative result for this slice. This is a configuration decision, not a cross-model superiority claim.
## Budgets, isolation, and fairness

- Fresh session at every receiver checkpoint; no hidden session persistence.
- Identical Harvey tools, source workspace, role prompt template, timeout, and output schema across multi-agent arms.
- Pair arms by task/model/attempt seed or attempt order where the provider exposes no seed. Randomize arm order within each pair.
- C1 and C2 share the same mutable ordinary `coordination.md`, source workspace, worker prompts, artifact schema, tool/action caps, roles, and centralized fan-out/synthesis schedule. C1 must contain no Proofpress metadata or verification signal.
- C2 retains every ordinary C1 coordination channel. It additionally embeds verified Proofpress lineage in key worker findings, adoption/rejection/merge decisions, and final artifacts; it does not use an external `provenance.md` treatment sidecar.
- B0 is Harvey's original one-agent continuous session: no SAS handoff, Proofpress metadata, ARA input, or raw transcript is injected or persisted. C0 and C3 use the same five fixed fresh-session SAS checkpoints (plan, evidence, decision, draft, review) with one homogeneous role and the same task, tools, prompt contract, and caps. C0 receives ordinary checkpoint continuity. C3 adds only system-scheduled native Proofpress admission: the agent supplies semantic content, deterministic code validates and commits it, and the receiver reads latest admitted artifact heads plus the final-artifact index rather than a transcript or sidecar.
- Each trial has the same total billable input-plus-output token cap. Worker prompts, repeated source context, ordinary coordination text, Proofpress metadata, and tool output all count. Do not use meaningless padding to match bytes.
- Record separate token categories: task/evidence content, ordinary coordination, Proofpress metadata, and tool/transport overhead, plus tool calls, wall time, and estimated cost.
- Use the concrete Gateway model slug, a qualification-derived provider allowlist, no fallback during formal runs, and fixed effort/temperature. Record Gateway response metadata and resolved provider rather than assuming the request ID is sufficient. A workflow with incomplete model/provider/cost/fallback telemetry is not qualified for analysis.
- The Proofpress capsule is verified before presentation. A tampered/stripped capsule must be classified as invalid or ordinary artifact, never as admitted lineage.
- A receiver may reverse a prior decision only with new evidence or a recorded reversal condition; all arms receive the same opportunity.
- Raw prompts, source documents, full traces, credentials, and restricted benchmark material stay in `PROOFPRESS_EVAL_HOME`, outside Git.
## Outcomes and scoring

The primary outcome for the next slice is **per-criterion Harvey success rate**, reported paired by task and arm with its numerator and denominator. Harvey official all-pass remains a hard-task diagnostic and secondary outcome: `0/36` in the completed transport prototype is expectedly uninformative for continuous quality comparison because every criterion must pass. `trusted_task_success` remains a safety/trust composite, not a substitute for the criterion table.

| Dimension | Measure | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Task quality | per-criterion pass rate (primary for Harvey); current-conclusion accuracy and successful terminal artifact (dynamic) | fixed scorer + gold decision sheet |
| Trust | decision regression, unsupported authority upgrade, correct reversal, false block, source/claim fidelity | deterministic checks + blinded audit |
| Continuity and lineage | stale-conclusion misuse, evidence-to-claim coverage, decision-lineage completeness, session-restart recovery, correct revision/reversal | replay oracle + Proofpress verifier + blinded audit |
| Efficiency | input/output tokens, wall time, cost estimate, tool calls, history reads, token cost per successful task | harness and wrapper records |
| Provenance integrity | capsule verification, artifact hash continuity, declared actor/status agreement | Proofpress verifier |

The official rubric should run blindly to arm labels. A second blinded judge and a human audit of at least 20% of sampled runs assess provenance-specific annotations. Report inter-rater agreement (target Cohen's κ ≥ 0.70) rather than presenting an unvalidated judge as ground truth.
## Analysis and decision gates

Analyze the primary paired contrast with task and model effects, and report episode-cluster bootstrap confidence intervals. For binary trusted success, use a mixed or fixed-effects logistic model only if the sample supports it; otherwise report paired rates and stratified uncertainty without overclaiming significance. Always publish per-model and per-task plots alongside aggregates.

| Gate | Pass condition | Stop / revise condition |
|---|---|---|
| Completed 1a/1b transport prototype | 24/24 Gate 1a receiver calls and 36/36 clean workflow records establish runtime feasibility | do not interpret sidecar memory versus `provenance.md` as native-product efficacy |
| B0 baseline | the independent one-shot workflow has preflight/scorer output and complete per-call model/provider/cost/fallback telemetry | retain its audit result separately; do not add it to the C0/C3 qualification verdict |
| Gateway SAS qualification | both C0/C3 workflows have valid carriers/preflight/scorer output and complete per-call model/provider/cost/fallback telemetry | repair adapter or stop; do not substitute an unversioned model or missing cost |
| Harvey formal matrix | 12 completed workflows, paired C3−C0 report, and no trust/reversal harm or budget excess | do not pool historical transport records or scale a broken qualification |
| STATE-Bench + MemConflict | each benchmark has its own frozen task/scorer gate and an interpretable C3−C0 report | keep results independent; stop if continuity failure mode is absent |
| HiEviDR-Bench + DeepResearch Bench | adapter/scorer gate passes before any external-validity run | repair the benchmark adapter rather than infer from Harvey |
The numerical threshold for Gate 2 will be locked after Gate 0 calibrates score variance and before Gate 1 is run. This avoids inventing a significance threshold from an unvalidated local fixture.
## Implementation milestones

1. Archive Gate 1a/1b as the external-transport prototype, including its criterion-level diagnostic and operational failures.
2. Freeze and run the isolated PSA Gateway C0/C3 qualification with five serial SAS checkpoints, native C3 carriers, final-output preflight, full Gateway telemetry, and a $25 shared actual-cost ceiling.
3. If and only if both workflows qualify, freeze a separate provider-allowlist/no-fallback configuration for the 12-workflow Harvey matrix; otherwise repair the adapter without reinterpreting qualification records.
4. Use ARA to manage paper evidence and Proofpress to snapshot meaningful accepted research artifacts—not every chat turn or raw transcript.
## Completed APEX-derived Law Artifact Handoff Track (public-source negative control)

**Purpose and label.** This is a derived, two-stage artifact-handoff experiment built from APEX Law task `task_323b4e29af5e4c7f86eaf4a24c4487ad`, not a modification of the official one-stage benchmark and not an official APEX score. The preflight native Gemini run was `4/6`: a revision artifact exists and four substantive facts survived, but two mandated terminology corrections regressed. Finance is excluded because its completed Gemini qualifications exposed a one-agent source-authority floor, not a handoff mechanism.

**Task contract.** Agent A works in a clean official Law world, reviews the existing certificate, lease, and correspondence, and creates an initial decision artifact plus private review notes. Freeze only A's final handoff information. Agent B starts in a new clean Law world with all normal public APEX resources, but never A's private scratchpad/session. B receives a fixed follow-on instruction: produce `Deliverables/Estoppel Certificate Revision 2.docx`, correct the remaining `Tenant` → `Lessee` and `Landlord` → `Lessor` terminology consistently, preserve the four validated substantive positions, and provide a short change log. This makes public-source retrieval ordinary rather than artificially forbidden; the experimentally relevant continuity object is A's reviewed issue-to-change mapping.

**Arms and semantic-parity gate.** The ordinary package is a readable portable handoff containing the current artifact location, reviewed facts, conclusions, outstanding corrections, and next actions. The Proofpress package contains exactly the same normalized fact/conclusion/action text plus native anchors, admitted head, evidence-to-decision links, and an independently verifiable capsule. Before any B run, compare normalized package text and a fact inventory; any extra fact, conclusion, or action in either package invalidates the pair. Both arms use Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, identical public world/task hash, tools, time and step caps, and no access to A's private scratchpad. The only allowed variable is provenance/verification structure.

**Execution and scoring.** Execute three ordinary and three Proofpress B runs serially, each from a fresh world, in randomized order under neutral run IDs. Preflight the Gemini tool-call path once; record provider/model, image/config/world hashes, dataset revision, trajectory, final snapshot, native grades, watchdog state, package-parity evidence, capsule-verification result, and condition manifest. The original APEX native rubric is retained as a final-artifact quality gate, but the primary derived outcome is a condition-blind seven-item revision audit: artifact present; each of the two terminology corrections complete; each of the four validated substantive positions preserved; and no contradiction introduced. Record native rubric pass rate, derived audit pass rate, trusted success, regression count, and infrastructure/model aborts separately.

**Interpretation and decision gate.** Report all six complete runs with numerator/denominator and uncertainty; never turn a 3+3 difference into a confirmed general effect. Continue only if the ordinary arm has observable correction/regression error, package parity holds, capsules verify independently, and Proofpress improves or preserves trusted success without a semantic-information advantage. A null result is still informative for this Law calibration: because Agent B can read every original source, it would show that provenance did not add measurable value on this public-source revision boundary. Any broader efficacy claim requires another revision/update task in which the handoff carries genuine, reviewed, non-public Agent A work while ordinary public resources remain available.

**Completed calibration (2026-08-09).** The precommitted 3+3 completed without an infrastructure abort: all three upstream reviews and all six receivers produced a trajectory, final snapshot, native grades, and a completed watchdog state. Native receiver outcomes were identical by arm: ordinary `4/6, 6/6, 4/6` and Proofpress `4/6, 6/6, 4/6` (mean `4.67/6`, or `77.8%`, in each arm). The condition-blind seven-cell audits were likewise identical: ordinary `3/7, 7/7, 5/7` and Proofpress `3/7, 7/7, 5/7` (mean `5.0/7`, or `71.4%`, in each arm). Pair 2 repaired a `4/6` upstream artifact to `6/6`; pair 3 repaired a `2/6` upstream artifact to `4/6` in both arms. Every Proofpress capsule verified independently, while each ordinary package had the same semantic-handoff SHA-256 and was correctly recorded as `not_applicable` for capsule verification.

**Decision.** This is a calibrated null result, not evidence that Proofpress harms or improves Law-task outcome quality. Both arms repaired the same error space equally, and the public-source Law world leaves Agent B able to independently reconstruct the source facts. The result validates the two-stage runner, parity lock, provenance capsule verification, final-snapshot native grading, and audit collection; it does not establish a Proofpress efficacy effect. Do not expand this task. Select a new revision/update task where Agent A's reviewed work supplies genuine continuity value beyond sources public to Agent B, and make the native judge condition-blind to package filenames before the next efficacy track.
## Completed APEX-derived Restricted-Access Artifact Handoff Track

**Purpose, estimand, and real-world boundary.** This derived two-stage Lease experiment estimates `Proofpress − ordinary` only when a receiver starts in a fresh restricted world with the same semantic handoff but cannot re-enter Agent A's source workspace. It is a cross-boundary/cross-world handoff study, not an official APEX score, a general handoff estimate, or an interoperability result across heterogeneous agent systems. The restricted condition models a real access discontinuity—principally a deal-room access window closing or being revoked, with confidentiality boundaries and third-party workspace expiry as related cases. It does not claim that the organization destroyed the source record; it limits only the receiver's access path.

**Receiver contract and access audit.** Agent A works in a fresh complete official Lease world. Each Agent B starts from a separately materialized restricted receiver snapshot containing only the current redraft, its handoff package, and the same task goal and normal tool budget. The snapshot excludes the lease, amendment, correspondence, certificate source bundle, `.apps_data`, archives, source filenames, Agent A trajectory, and private scratchpad. Before every scored pair, an automated leakage preflight must prove that each denied path is unreadable, unlistable, and unrecoverable from an archive or app-state residue. A failure is a boundary failure, not an outcome.

**Matched carrier contrast.** Ordinary handoff is the current artifact plus a readable memory/log/handoff message. The Proofpress handoff carries exactly the same normalized facts, conclusions, outstanding work, and next actions in the artifact, adding only native anchors, admitted head, declared decision lineage, and a verification capsule. Every pair must record an identical `semantic_handoff_sha256` and draft hash; an information mismatch invalidates the pair. Capsule verification establishes artifact identity, integrity, and the declared decision lineage. It does not establish that an inaccessible source fact is true or complete.

**Pilot, scoring, and interpretation.** Begin with one upstream A and one ordinary/one Proofpress B. The follow-on instruction asks B to complete outstanding revisions and produce a short change log, without naming the terminology substitutions or substantive answers. Grade only the final DOCX through a neutral, arm-blind package; keep a separate independent seven-cell artifact audit. The 1+1 pilot must pass leakage, semantic-parity, capsule, blind-layout, model/Docker/watchdog, and receiver-completion gates before serial randomized 3+3 begins. Report native rubric pass, audit pass, trusted success, regressions/missed corrections, and capsule status separately. A result applies only to this restricted-access Lease condition; the completed public-source 3+3 is not a matched full-access cell and cannot identify an access-condition interaction.

**Completed boundary pilot and serial 3+3 (2026-08-09).** An initial formal r1 was invalidated before primary analysis when pair 2's handoff disclosed an original source filename; it is retained only as boundary-debugging evidence. The repaired filename preflight then passed a fresh r4 1+1 pilot: semantic and draft hashes matched, the Proofpress capsule verified, both B worlds completed, neutral final-DOCX-only judging was used, and both runtime-leakage audits passed. The fresh r2 serial 3+3 then completed all six B runs under Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, a 300-second call limit, and a 3,900-second watchdog. Every pair passed semantic/draft parity, preflight, capsule (Proofpress), receiver-completion, and runtime-leakage gates; all native judges consumed the arm-neutral final-DOCX package only.

**Results, measurement correction, and decision.** Native rubric cells were Proofpress `10/18` (mean `0.556`) versus ordinary `9/18` (mean `0.500`); one Proofpress run, and no ordinary run, achieved a perfect native `6/6`. The frozen v1 seven-cell audit reported a `13/21` tie, but post-run inspection found that it scanned the entire DOCX rather than the operative certificate, lowercased defined-party terms so generic phrases counted as failures, and allowed prefatory analysis to satisfy certificate cells. A separately versioned post-hoc v2 audit, scoped to the operative certificate and ineligible as a confirmatory endpoint, reports Proofpress `17/21` versus ordinary `16/21`; the same single terminology cell accounts for the native and v2 differences. The Lease result remains bounded and inconclusive: the correction removes the claimed independent tie but does not turn a post-hoc one-cell contrast into a reliable effect. Do not add Lease runs.
## Preregistered next task: restricted-access S-Corp SPA revision

**Task choice.** The next candidate is APEX task `task_8705d28530a94c2880fbfd7190e257d4` (`World425_jcf_01`), which edits an existing Stock Purchase Agreement across nine clause-level buyer-protection requirements covering representations, warranties, pre-closing obligations, post-closing cooperation, liability allocation, and indemnity. It was selected before any receiver outcome because it has a persistent transaction artifact, a large diligence workspace, multiple interdependent revision targets, and materially more error space than the Lease terminology cleanup. The task/world hashes and full protocol are frozen in `configs/frozen/apex-scorp-spa-revision-pilot-v1/preregistration.json`.

**Carrier and measurement repair.** Both arms receive the same current SPA and normalized facts, decisions, clause targets, status, and next actions. Proofpress may add only anchored decision blocks, admitted status and supersession, clause links, the current-SPA binding digest, and a verifiable capsule. Unlike the Lease carrier's heading/hash-only metadata, each lineage item must identify an actionable clause target and implementation state. The primary scorer must be scoped to named operative SPA sections and pass positive, negative, prefatory-analysis, capitalization, and unrelated-clause-regression fixtures before any model call.

**Authorization gate.** Only a single upstream A plus paired randomized 1+1 receiver pilot is authorized after all source-hash, parity, scorer-fixture, capsule, blind-layout, and leakage preflights pass. The formal 3+3 remains unauthorized. A pilot failure repairs the protocol and is not counted; a clean pilot proceeds only if ordinary has eligible clause-level error space and neither arm has semantic-information advantage.

**Methodological precedent, not a boundary claim.** ARA's PaperBench reproduction evaluation is the closest design reference for fair representation comparison: it holds model, task, tools, and budget fixed, masks directly copyable expected numeric results, and applies blind requirement-level grading to a structured artifact versus PDF-plus-repository baseline. That supports this track's matched carrier, neutral-prompt, and blind-artifact principles. It does not validate the access-discontinuity estimand: ARA receivers can read the full ARA `logic/`, `src/`, `trace/`, and `evidence/` package, whereas this Lease receiver is intentionally limited to the current artifact and handoff. Proofpress therefore studies a narrower successor-continuity question, not whether ARA's full research package is better.
